subject: astronomy
title: Phases & Tides: The Moon's Pull
welcome_lead: The Moon's gravity tugs the ocean — and gives us tides twice a day.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: tides caused by Moon's gravity, high/low tide.
final_note: When the Moon pulls, the ocean answers.

concepts.def: Daily rise and fall of the sea.
Bigger tide near new and full Moon.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Moon's gravity pulls the side of Earth facing it. The ocean bulges toward the Moon. Inertia leaves a matching bulge on the far side.
As Earth rotates through these two bulges, most coasts get two high tides and two low tides a day.
When the Sun, Earth and Moon line up at new or full Moon, tides are larger — spring tides. At half Moon they pull at right angles, giving smaller neap tides.
